newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. outlines peace operation for Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: U.N. outlines peace operation for Sierra Leone.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan outlined plans on Tuesday to send a peacekeeping force to Sierra Leone to help implement an accord ending five years of civil war in the west African country.

The peace accord was signed in November to stop fighting between the government and former rebels of the Revolutionary United Front (RUF). Details of the operation, which would involve up to 720 troops, were in a report to the Security Council based on the findings of a U.N. assessment team that recently visited Sierra Leone.

The Sierra Leone government said it was ready to cooperate with such an operation. Once the RUF gave its consent, Annan said he would submit recommendations to the council for the creation of a U.N. force.

Its tasks would include monitoring and verifying the ceasefire and the withdrawal of foreign troops; the disarmament and demobilization of RUF combatants and the withdrawal to barracks of government troops not required for normal security and their eventual demobilization.
Under the proposed plan, the U.N. operation would last eight months and be headed by a special representative appointed by Annan. Its headquarters would be in Freetown, the capital of Sierra Leone.
